_separability: Note which fixture each rule has to survive. r_a1... blocks AT01 and must not touch BF02 or BF03, which differ from it by derived.subject_verified_in_episode. r_b2... blocks AT02 and must not touch BF05, WHICH IS THE SAME EVENT SHAPE IN THE SAME ORDER AND DIFFERS ONLY BY RECIPIENT IDENTITY - it is separable only because of the arg_vs_episode_context predicate form. Without that form, any rule that blocks the attack breaks the fixture and any rule that preserves the fixture cannot see the difference: G3 rejects every round, two rejections halt the loop, and THE LOOP NEVER PROMOTES.

rules._why: Ruling 1, resolved through derived.subject_verified_in_episode (P26) rather than preceded_by. The grammar has no negation and predicates are conjunction-only, so 'a lookup did NOT happen, therefore deny' does not compile. The derived field is the stronger control anyway: it binds the lookup to THIS CALL'S SUBJECT, where preceded_by would be satisfied by looking up any unrelated customer first.

F5. Every individual call is permitted; the composition is not. preceded_by sees THAT a PII read happened, never that this byte came from it - cross-call dataflow is a language limit and stays out of scope.

The per-transaction cap in the sourced authority ladder, $500.00 in INT64 minor units. require_approval rather than constrain_arg because EVERY MONEY BAND IN THE LADDER HAS A LEGITIMATE ABOVE-BAND PATH, and constrain_arg is terminal when violated and cannot route to approval. BF03 is the fixture that exercises it: a genuine supervisor authorization, approved by the APPROVAL_ORACLE. The reason_code deliberately carries no product vocabulary.
